new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the final syllable of the word; that syllable is where all the segmental, laryngeal and tonal contrasts are expressed (nasal and laryngealized vowels, central vowels, pre-glottalized/pre-nasalized onsets, phonemic tone, phonetic vowel lengthening all restricted to the final syllable). Corroborated by the JIPA Illustration (Elliott, Edmondson & Sandoval Cruz 2016: 353), which transcribes the Spanish loan lápiz as [la3ˈpi3h] and states that 'stress is shifted from the penultimate to the ultimate syllable', and by Matsukawa 2009 fn. 3 ('a plain vowel is phonetically lengthened in a final syllable').
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated for stress. Spanish loanwords are adapted to final stress (JIPA 2016: 353: lápiz > [la3ˈpi3h]; polysyllabic loans lengthen the final vowel). Phonemic tone is otherwise final-syllable only, but future/past aspect forms carry contrastive tone on a non-final syllable (LD&C 2012: 216; JIPA 2016: 360).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (phonological word including fused enclitics; Matsukawa's statement is made within the phonotactics of the word and generalised to 'Triqui languages'). The statement is a one-clause aside, not a dedicated stress section; the dissertation has no prosody/stress chapter (TOC checked). No instrumental study of stress in this variety was found.
new_statements.identity_note: Matsukawa 2012 describes Chicahuaxtla Triqui (chic1273) from speakers of La Laguna Guadalupe and San Andrés Chicahuaxtla (diss. pp. 21-24); the JIPA Illustration (Elliott, Edmondson & Sandoval Cruz 2016) is based on a San Andrés Chicahuaxtla speaker. Both are the same language-level entry; no dialect split needed. Sister languages Copala Triqui (copa1237) and Itunyoso Triqui (itun1250) are already in the catalog with final prominence.

[...] The word [la3ˈpi3h] ‘pencil’, from Spanish lápiz [ˈla.pis], retains the original

new_statements.quote: 2. The WORD in SAC Trique is also well-marked. The ultima is the position of phonemic differentiation, and nonultimas are positions of neutralization. The contrast between fortis and lenis consonants, for example, occurs only in ultimas and is neutralized in nonultimas. In addition, a far greater range of tonal possibilities occurs in ultimas than in nonultimas. Words have stress on the ultima. There is also a phonetic stress on a penult with tone 2, and on a penult preceding an ultima with a medially-checked vowel (VʔV or VhV).

new_statements.rule_in_words: In San Andrés Chicahuaxtla Trique the word is stressed on its final syllable (ultima), which is also the locus of segmental and tonal contrast; non-final syllables are positions of neutralization. The language is tonal (five-register system, all syllables carry tone) and the author states stress explicitly alongside tone.
new_statements.secondary_stress: A non-contrastive 'phonetic stress' also falls on a penult that bears tone 2, and on a penult that precedes an ultima with a medially checked vowel (VʔV or VhV).
new_statements.exceptions: Only the phonetic penult stress cases above; section 2.4 notes structure above the word in SAC 'has not been studied in detail' (vocative intonation contours replace tone on some kinship terms). For the other dialect, San Juan Copala (section 1.4, p. 49), stress is described at the phrase level: 'a stress on the ultima of the word which functions as its nucleus'.
new_statements.identity_note: Hollenbach 1977 covers two varieties: section 1 is San Juan Copala Trique (SJC = Copala Triqui, copa1237, where stress is described as phrase-level on the ultima of the nucleus word) and section 2 is San Andrés Chicahuaxtla Trique (SAC = this language, chic1273); only the SAC statements were related to the catalog. Matsukawa 2008 is about Chicahuaxtla Trique with comparative data from Copala and Itunyoso.

tone_statements.citation: Hernández Mendoza, Fidel. 2017. Tono y fonología segmental en el triqui de Chicahuaxtla. Tesis de maestría, UNAM. 388 pp.
tone_statements.quote: el inventario tonal del triqui de Chicahuaxtla consta de cinco tonos. (19) Inventario tonal del triqui de Chicahuaxtla Tono 5 extra alto 4 alto 3 medio 2 bajo 1 extra bajo Estos tonos representan cinco niveles contrastivos de tonía. Siguiendo la terminología usada en el análisis tonal (Yip 2002), pueden ser clasificados como tonos de nivel. Estos cinco tonos se combinan para dar lugar a diez tonos básicos contrastivos en el plano de la sílaba: /1/, /2/, /3/, /4/, /35/, /13/, /23/, /43/, /32/ y /31/ cuyo estatus se discute en §6.3.
tone_statements.translation: the tonal inventory of Chicahuaxtla Triqui consists of five tones. (19) Tonal inventory of Chicahuaxtla Triqui: Tone 5 extra high, 4 high, 3 mid, 2 low, 1 extra low. These tones represent five contrastive pitch levels. Following the terminology used in tonal analysis (Yip 2002), they can be classified as level tones. These five tones combine to give ten basic contrastive tones at the level of the syllable: /1/, /2/, /3/, /4/, /35/, /13/, /23/, /43/, /32/ and /31/, whose status is discussed in sec. 6.3.
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Five level tones (1 extra-low to 5 extra-high); contours are level sequences, giving ten syllable tones (4 level, 3 rising, 3 falling; sec. 6.3, F0 tracks). TBU mora; tone patterns assigned to roots. Fixed final stress; full tone contrasts only on the stressed syllable. Floating NP boundary tone.

tone_statements.quote: El inventario preliminar de los tonos del triqui de Chicahuaxtla que aquí se propone consta de 5 tonos de nivel, 3 tonos de contorno simple y 2 tonos de contorno complejo, todos analizados en palabras aisladas. Los tonos de nivel 1, 2, 3 y 4 se realizan con una tonía estable, en cambio, el tono 5, fonéticamente un tono [353] o [53]. [...] Si bien la lengua distingue un gran número de tonos, su distribución contrastiva está condicionada por la prominencia silábica. En sílaba prominente puede ocurrir cualquiera de los tonos que conforman el inventario tonal, en cambio, en sílaba no prominente solamente tonos de nivel.
tone_statements.translation: The preliminary inventory of Chicahuaxtla Triqui tones proposed here consists of 5 level tones, 3 simple contour tones and 2 complex contour tones, all analysed in isolated words. Level tones 1, 2, 3 and 4 are realised with stable pitch, whereas tone 5 is phonetically [353] or [53]. [...] Although the language distinguishes a large number of tones, their contrastive distribution is conditioned by syllable prominence. Any tone of the inventory may occur in a prominent syllable, whereas only level tones occur in a non-prominent syllable.

tone.quote: el inventario tonal del triqui de Chicahuaxtla consta de cinco tonos. (19) Inventario tonal del triqui de Chicahuaxtla Tono 5 extra alto 4 alto 3 medio 2 bajo 1 extra bajo Estos tonos representan cinco niveles contrastivos de tonía. Siguiendo la terminología usada en el análisis tonal (Yip 2002), pueden ser clasificados como tonos de nivel. Estos cinco tonos se combinan para dar lugar a diez tonos básicos contrastivos en el plano de la sílaba: /1/, /2/, /3/, /4/, /35/, /13/, /23/, /43/, /32/ y /31/ cuyo estatus se discute en §6.3.
tone.translation: the tonal inventory of Chicahuaxtla Triqui consists of five tones. (19) Tonal inventory of Chicahuaxtla Triqui: Tone 5 extra high, 4 high, 3 mid, 2 low, 1 extra low. These tones represent five contrastive pitch levels. Following the terminology used in tonal analysis (Yip 2002), they can be classified as level tones. These five tones combine to give ten basic contrastive tones at the level of the syllable: /1/, /2/, /3/, /4/, /35/, /13/, /23/, /43/, /32/ and /31/, whose status is discussed in sec. 6.3.
tone.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone.summary: Five level tones (1 extra-low to 5 extra-high); contours are level sequences, giving ten syllable tones (4 level, 3 rising, 3 falling; sec. 6.3, F0 tracks). TBU mora; tone patterns assigned to roots. Fixed final stress; full tone contrasts only on the stressed syllable. Floating NP boundary tone.
